Santiago Vega’s approach to quality assurance stood out during his internship with our team. When a client’s API integration failed under load, he spearheaded a refactor of their test suite using BDD frameworks. By aligning test scenarios with business rules, he reduced regression errors by 40% and clarified requirements for stakeholders. His ability to translate ambiguity into actionable tests was critical to resolving the issue before the project deadline.  

As a professor, I’ve collaborated with Santiago on two consulting projects. He consistently bridges academic rigor with real-world problem-solving. During a healthcare platform audit, he designed Selenium scripts that uncovered a critical data validation flaw, preventing a potential compliance risk. His work ethic is meticulous—once, he spent 12 hours debugging a flaky test, ultimately isolating a race condition in the UI flow.  

Santiago’s strength lies in his ownership of test frameworks. He doesn’t just execute tests; he architects them. In one instance, he restructured a legacy test suite into modular, reusable components, cutting maintenance time by 30%. His curiosity drives him to ask “why” behind every failure, which elevates team problem-solving.  

In summary, Santiago is a dependable, detail-oriented engineer who thrives in complex, dynamic environments. His technical depth and collaborative mindset make him a valuable asset.
